info.title: Agentic Commerce API
info.summary: Frontend↔backend contract for the Agentic Commerce UI.
info.description:
Every operation in this document is a thin HTTP wrapper over a function that **already exists** in the Python package, named in each operation's `x-backs-onto` field. The domain layer already returns structured data (`WebResult.as_dict`, `CrewEvent.as_dict`, `BestPick.as_dict`, `PaymentResult.as_dict`, `NegotiationResult.as_dict`, raw UCP product dicts, signed AP2 mandate dicts); only the LangChain *tool* layer wraps those in Markdown for the model to read. This API calls the domain layer directly and skips the Markdown, so a new UI can be built in any stack with **no changes to the agent, crew, analyst, payments, or A2A code**.

## Honesty invariants the client must respect

These are not stylistic. They are encoded in the backend and the UI must not contradict them.

1. **`PaymentResult.live` is always present.** `backend/payments.py` refuses any key that is not `rzp_test_*` / `sk_test_*`, so a payment is test-mode or simulated. A receipt that does not say so is a bug.
2. **`ProductScore.missing` is required.** A criterion the Analyst could not score is *unknown*, not zero. Rendering a missing rating as an empty star row misstates the data.
3. **`BestPick.caveat` must be surfaced.** The UCP catalog exposes **no purchase-volume field**. Review count is a popularity proxy; no label may imply units sold.
4. **`WebResult` is not purchasable.** External listings cannot enter a Universal Cart. Clients render no cart affordance on them — absence, not a disabled button.

## Streaming

`POST /api/chat/stream` is Server-Sent Events. OpenAPI cannot fully describe SSE framing, so the response is declared as `text/event-stream` and each event payload is defined as a named schema under the `StreamEvent` `oneOf`, discriminated on `type`. Those event names are not invented for this document — they are the vocabulary `CommerceAgent.execute_stream` already emits, plus `crew` from `CommerceCrew.stream_events`.

## Known defect affecting this contract

`backend/agent.py:252` uses `return` where it must `yield` inside the `execute_stream` generator, which terminates the stream on the first text token. Until that is fixed, `/api/chat/stream` will emit `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`products` events for tool-first turns but will drop `content` events and end the turn early for conversational replies. See `ui_enhancement.md` Part 0.

get.description: Reports which payment provider would be selected and whether a web-search API key is configured, so the UI can set expectations before the shopper hits a dead end.
Mirrors `MODEL_CHOICES` in `ui/app.py`: the `MODEL` environment default first, then the common tiers.

post.summary: Send a message and stream the agent's work as Server-Sent Events.
post.description:
Wraps `CommerceAgent.execute_stream`. The response is `text/event-stream`; each SSE `data:` line is one JSON object matching `StreamEvent`.

**Ordering guarantees**

- `status` may appear at any point; it is advisory text only.
- Every `tool_call` is followed by exactly one `tool_result` for the same `tool`.
- `products` follows the `tool_result` of a tool that changed the result set (`search_products`, `get_product_details`, `pick_best_product`).
- `content` events are token deltas and must be **concatenated in arrival order**; they are not whole messages.
- `crew` events from parallel specialists **interleave**. Do not infer sequencing from arrival order — use `agent` to route each event to its own row and `duration` for elapsed time. Two scouts running concurrently will emit `running` for both before either emits `done`; rendering them as sequential would misrepresent the system.
- `done` is always the final event of a successful turn. `error` is terminal.

**Cancellation:** closing the connection aborts the turn. Any tool already in flight completes server-side, so partial state may still be written to the session.

Session resolution order: the request body, then the `ac_session` cookie, then a freshly minted id. The response sets `ac_session` (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) and echoes the id in `X-Session-Id` and in the `done` event, so a client that keeps the id in local storage and one that relies on the cookie both survive a refresh. The id is a capability token for a durable session (`backend/session_store.py`).

X-Accel-Buffering.description: Set to `no` so reverse proxies do not buffer the stream.

parallelDiscovery.summary: Two scouts running concurrently, then an answer

get.summary: Full snapshot of everything the UI renders outside the transcript.
get.description:
One call rehydrates the results grid, gallery, cart badge, best-pick ribbon, and payment receipt — used on page load and after reconnecting a dropped stream.

**Caveat:** sessions are currently held in a process-local dict (`_SESSION_STORE`), so a server restart empties them and a horizontally-scaled deployment will not share them. See `ui_enhancement.md` §1.1.

delete.summary: Clear search results, web results, active product, and best-pick verdict.
delete.description: Backs the "Clear" control. Clears every source the gallery reads from, including `active_product` and `best_pick` — leaving either set makes the grid repopulate on the next render, which is the bug this method was written to prevent. Does **not** clear the cart or mandate.

post.summary: Search the Shopify UCP Global Catalog.
post.description: Direct catalog search with no LLM in the loop — use for filter and sort refinements so changing a price cap does not cost a model round-trip. Results are written into the session.

post.summary: Search the open web for listings the catalog does not carry.
post.description:
Uses Tavily when `TAVILY_API_KEY` is set, otherwise the keyless DuckDuckGo Lite endpoint. With `with_images=true` each result is enriched concurrently with its `og:image`/`twitter:image`; retailer category pages routinely omit those tags, so `image_url` is frequently `null` and `favicon_url` is the fallback.

Results are **not purchasable** — see the `WebResult` schema.

post.summary: Run both scouts in parallel and return their combined report.
post.description:
Fans `CatalogScout` and `WebScout` out with `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)`, so total latency tracks the slower scout rather than their sum and one failing scout never cancels the other.

Web results are held back when the catalog returned at least `thin_result_threshold` (default 3) hits, so a healthy catalog result is not buried under external links; the `events` array records that decision. **Render `events` — they are the data behind the agent-activity surface, and error events here are the only way a client can distinguish "nothing matched" from "the provider failed".**

get.summary: Full product detail, optionally filtered to a chosen variant.
get.description: When `selected` is supplied (e.g. `Color=Black`), the response's `media` is variant-filtered per the UCP spec — this is how the image filmstrip shows the right colourway rather than the default one.

post.summary: Rank a result set and name the best fit for a stated need.
post.description:
Deterministic scoring — the same products and the same `need` always produce the same verdict, so the UI can explain *why* something won.

**Scoring rules the client must render faithfully:**

- A criterion with no data is dropped and the remaining weights are renormalized. It appears in `missing[]`. It is **not** scored as zero, and must not be drawn as an empty rating.
- `fabric_fit` is skipped entirely when `need` states no material-relevant trait — pass the shopper's own phrasing, not a bare product name.
- Prices are compared only within one currency; a product priced in another reports `price_value` under `missing[]` rather than being ranked against it.
- `caveat` explains that popularity is inferred from review count. The catalog has no purchase-volume field.

statedNeed.summary: Need phrased in the shopper's words

409.description: No candidate products — run a search first.

post.summary: Negotiate a price via A2A against the merchant agent.
post.description: Runs `RFQ → OFFER → COUNTER…` until `ACCEPT`/`REJECT` or `max_rounds`. The buyer agent enforces `budget_cents` as a hard ceiling and the merchant enforces a private floor, so an agreed price is never above the stated budget. The full `transcript` is returned for audit — surface it behind a disclosure rather than in the main flow.

post.summary: Create a Universal Cart on the merchant's Storefront MCP server.
post.description: Discovers the merchant's MCP endpoint via `/.well-known/ucp`, then creates the cart. Only catalog variants are valid here — a `WebResult` has no variant id and cannot be carted.

parameters.name: merchant_domain
parameters.description: Merchant storefront domain the cart belongs to.

get.summary: Re-read a cart's current contents and totals.

post.summary: Convert a cart into a checkout session or an attributed referral link.
post.description: Falls back to the merchant's cart permalink when the MCP checkout call is unavailable, so `continue_url` is always populated with something the shopper can open.

post.summary: Generate a signed AP2 payment authorization mandate.
post.description: Produces an HMAC-SHA256 signed mandate scoped to one cart, one amount, and one expiry. `spending_limit_cents` equals `amount_cents` — the mandate authorizes exactly the cart total and no more. Show the shopper `amount_cents`, `expires_at`, and `status` before they act on it; the `signature` is for verification, not display.

Provider chain: Razorpay if configured, else Stripe, else a simulated gateway. Any provider failure degrades to the simulated gateway so the shopper always gets a receipt.

**Safety guard:** `backend/payments.py` refuses any credential that is not a test key (`rzp_test_*`, `sk_test_*`) and raises `PaymentConfigurationError` rather than transacting on production credentials. An autonomous agent cannot move real money through this endpoint. `live` is therefore always `false` today, but it is on the wire because the client's rendering must depend on the response, not on an assumption.

400.description: Non-positive amount, or a non-test credential was configured.

get.summary: Token, tool, and latency stats for the session's latest turn.
Starter prompts, seeded from the live catalog.
get.description: Hard-coded examples go stale against a live catalog, and a first click that returns nothing is the worst first impression. Prompts are derived from titles the catalog carries now, cached for 10 minutes. `source` distinguishes a live sample (`catalog`) from the canned list used when the catalog is unreachable (`fallback`), so a client can avoid presenting stale suggestions as live ones.

post.summary: Re-check a mandate's signature and expiry.
post.description: The client holds a mandate it was handed over the wire; this proves what it is showing is still the authorization the server signed. Expired and tampered are reported as distinct reasons — collapsing them to "invalid" tells the shopper nothing about what to do next.

reason.description: Why it passed or failed, in words.

post.description: Starts a new session and repoints the `ac_session` cookie at it. The previous session is **not** deleted: it stays in the durable store under its own id, so "start over" costs the shopper nothing they might want back.

get.summary: The session as a knowledge graph, for context transfer.
get.description:
A transcript or a raw snapshot spends most of its tokens on prose and repeated JSON keys. This states each fact once against a short id (`P1`, `M1`, `C1`) and names the relationships that matter: which merchant sells a product, which cart a mandate authorizes, which mandate a payment settles.

`format=text` returns the line form meant for pasting into a prompt, with a legend so a model that has not seen the format can read it. `format=json` adds the nodes and edges. Token counts are character-based estimates, not a tokenizer's output.

Honesty markers survive the compression: an unrated product carries no rating rather than a zero, a web result is flagged non-purchasable, a payment states `live`, and the Analyst's unscored criteria are listed.

estimated_tokens_raw_snapshot.description: Same session as a raw snapshot, for comparison.

graph.description: Nodes and edges; only when format=json.

sessionCookie.name: ac_session
sessionCookie.description: Opaque session identifier. **This is a capability token**: anyone holding it can read the associated cart, mandate, and payment history. Issue unguessable values, set `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` outside local development. Never derive it from anything guessable or user-supplied.

SessionId.name: sessionId
SessionId.description: Session identifier. Treat as a capability token — see `sessionCookie`.

RateLimited.description: Upstream model or search provider rate limit reached.

UpstreamError.description: The UCP catalog, merchant MCP server, or search provider failed.

payment_provider.description: Which provider `select_provider()` would choose right now.

Money.description: An amount in **minor units** (cents/pence) plus its ISO-4217 currency. Never compare amounts across currencies.

alt_text.description: Use as the image `alt`; fall back to the product title when absent.

Rating.description: Present on some products, and on **variants only** for other merchants — clients must check both, as `analyst._rating_of` does. Absence means *not rated*, not badly rated.

count.description: Number of reviews. A popularity proxy only — never a sales figure.

RichText.description: Either a plain string or a `{plain, html}` object, depending on merchant. Render `plain`; never inject `html` without sanitizing.

ProductMetadata.description: Merchant-authored copy. `tech_specs` is newline-delimited `Key: Value` pairs and is where the `Fabric:` line lives — parse it with the same logic as `analyst.extract_fabric` rather than writing a second parser.

Product.description: A Shopify UCP Global Catalog product, passed through unmodified. Purchasable — unlike `WebResult`.

WebResult.description: An open-web listing. **Not purchasable** — it has no variant id and cannot enter a Universal Cart, so clients must render no cart affordance on it at all (absence, not a disabled control).

image_url.description: `og:image`/`twitter:image` when discoverable. Frequently `null` — retailer category pages routinely omit it.

favicon_url.description: Always populated. When `image_url` is null, render a distinct compact card rather than stretching this icon into a product-image slot.

CrewEvent.description: One progress report from a specialist agent. The unit of the agent-activity surface.

status.description: `filter` records a Concierge decision (e.g. holding web results back); `error` means this specialist failed while others may have succeeded.

duration.description: Seconds elapsed, on terminal events. Render this rather than a progress bar — completion percentage is unknowable.

web_results.description: Empty when the catalog returned at least `thin_result_threshold` hits — check `events` for the `filter` record explaining why.

weight.description: Renormalized so present criteria sum to 1.0 — not the base weight.

evidence.description: The literal reason, safe to display verbatim.

missing.description: Criteria that could not be scored, each with its reason. **Required rendering** — an unscored criterion is unknown, not zero, and hiding this list overstates the verdict's confidence.

need.description: The shopper's phrasing the verdict was judged against.

winner.description: Null when there were no candidates.

comparison.description: Why the winner beat each runner-up, in Markdown.

caveat.description: Must be surfaced. States that popularity is inferred from review count because the catalog exposes no purchase-volume field.
examples: popularity is inferred from review count; the UCP catalog exposes no purchase-volume field

savings_cents.description: How much the agreed price beat the opening offer.

live.description: Always `false` under the current test-key guard. **Required rendering:** a receipt must visibly state that no real money moved.

Cart.description: A UCP Universal Cart, passed through from the merchant's MCP server with `merchant_domain` added.

totals.description: Typed totals; the displayable one has `type: "total"`.

continue_url.description: Always populated — falls back to the merchant cart permalink when MCP checkout is unavailable.

expires_at.description: Unix epoch seconds. Show the shopper the remaining validity.

spending_limit_cents.description: Equals `amount_cents` — the mandate authorizes the cart total and nothing more.

signature.description: HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical mandate string. For verification, not display.

SessionSnapshot.description: Everything the UI renders outside the transcript. One call rehydrates the whole view.

best_pick.description: Cleared automatically whenever a new search runs — a stale verdict badged onto fresh results would be worse than none.

session_id.description: Omit to have the server mint one; it is returned on the `done` event.

history.description: Prior turns. Omit when the server-side session already holds them.

with_images.description: Enriches each result with its social preview image. Adds latency bounded by a short per-request timeout.

max_price.description: Major units (dollars), matching the crew's signature.

session_id.description: Scores the session's current results when `products` is omitted.

products.description: Explicit candidates, overriding the session's results.

need.description: The shopper's own phrasing. Fabric fit is skipped when this names no material-relevant trait, so a bare product name weakens the verdict.

budget_cents.description: Hard ceiling; the buyer agent never agrees above it.

receipt.description: Reference shown on the provider receipt.

ContentEvent.description: A token delta, not a whole message. Concatenate in arrival order.

result.description: Markdown written for the model to read. Show it behind a log toggle, not as primary UI — the structured equivalents are on the REST endpoints and in the session snapshot.

CrewStreamEvent.description: A `CrewEvent` on the wire. Events from concurrent specialists interleave — route by `agent`, do not infer order.

elapsed.description: Wall-clock seconds for the whole turn, measured server-side.

ErrorEvent.description: Terminal. The turn produced no further output.

ArtifactEvent.description: An object produced by the turn that is worth keeping rather than describing: an AP2 mandate or a payment receipt. Emitted once, at the moment the authorization or charge happens — not on every later turn while it exists. Clients render these inline in the transcript. A `payment` artifact always carries `live`, so the UI can state whether real money moved.
